summary: Target-level plan of Locally analytic distributions, growth, and character spaces, Part II: noncommutative distribution algebras and microlocalisation. It starts where LocallyAnalyticDistributions stops (function spaces and distributions on compact manifolds, abelian Mellin theory) and builds the noncommutative theory needed by Fu's sharp multiplicity bounds and by Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni. ND.0 develops p-valued groups, ordered bases, the condition (HYP), the analytic structure of p-valued groups, Lazard's Lie lattice and the first congruence subgroups of SL₂(ℤ_p). ND.1 constructs the distribution algebra D(G, K) under convolution, U(g_K) ⊂ D(G, K), the rational Iwasawa algebra inside it with its coefficient expansion, the finite free decomposition over open subgroups and the centrality of Z(g). ND.2 defines Fréchet–Stein algebras and coadmissible modules with Theorems A and B, the norms ‖·‖_r and Banach steps D_r(G, K), their graded rings and noetherianity, the Fréchet–Stein property of D(G, K) and its faithful flatness over the Iwasawa algebra (Schneider–Teitelbaum). ND.3 builds the completed enveloping algebras Û(h)_K, the closures U_r(g), Frommer's theorem, the crossed-product decomposition of D_{r_n} and the Arens–Michael envelope 𝒰(g) with its coadmissible modules. ND.4 develops algebraic microlocalisation, Lazard's m-adic filtration, the Ardakov–Wadsley theorem identifying the microlocalisation of R[[G]] with Û(g_R)_K and with D_{1/p}(G, K), coefficient extension, Lie modules and Fu's comparison of isotypic quotients. ND.5 treats infinitesimal characters, central strong duality, density of eigenfunctions, central quotients of the Banach steps, Ardakov–Brown's Ext comparison, faithfulness of affinoid Verma modules, and reaches Fu's Theorem 1.5: ℚ_p[[G]] → Û(g)_λ is injective for every λ ∈ ℤ_p^m. ND.6 supplies the Schneider–Teitelbaum duality between admissible Banach representations and finitely generated Iwasawa modules and the algebraic Peter–Weyl theorem for compact open subgroups of SL₂. Quasi-abelian and solid functional analysis is proposed as a separate Part II. Nothing is formalised.

nodes.title: p-valuations, ordered bases and the condition (HYP)
nodes.statement: Let G be a group and p a prime. A p-valuation on G is a function ω : G∖{1} → (1/(p−1), ∞) such that, with ω(1) := ∞, for all g, h ∈ G: ω(gh⁻¹) ≥ min(ω(g), ω(h)); ω(g⁻¹h⁻¹gh) ≥ ω(g) + ω(h); ω(g^p) = ω(g) + 1. For ν > 0 put G_ν = {g : ω(g) ≥ ν} and G_{ν+} = {g : ω(g) > ν}; these are normal subgroups and gr G = ⊕_{ν>0} G_ν/G_{ν+} is a graded Lie algebra over 𝔽_p[ε] (bracket from commutators, ε acting by g ↦ g^p, of degree 1). (G, ω) has finite rank d if gr G is a free 𝔽_p[ε]-module of rank d. An ordered basis is a sequence (h_1, …, h_d) in G∖{1} whose classes h_i G_{ω(h_i)+} form an 𝔽_p[ε]-basis of gr G. (G, ω) is saturated (p-saturated) if every g with ω(g) > p/(p−1) is a p-th power. The pair (G, ω) with a chosen ordered basis satisfies (HYP) if it is saturated and ω(h_i) + ω(h_j) > p/(p−1) for all i ≠ j.
hypotheses: ω is real valued; from ND.1 on it is assumed to take rational values, which is no loss of generality (Lazard III.3.1.11, as recalled in ST03 §4, p. 15).
At p = 2 the lower bound 1/(p−1) = 1 makes the axioms stronger; every statement of this roadmap that needs (HYP) is stated for odd p or with (HYP) as an explicit hypothesis.
proofSteps: G_ν and G_{ν+} are normal because ω is invariant under conjugation up to the commutator axiom: ω(ghg⁻¹) ≥ min(ω(h), ω(g)+ω(h)) = ω(h), and equality follows by symmetry (Schneider §23).

The commutator axiom makes [G_ν, G_μ] ⊆ G_{ν+μ}, which gives the graded Lie bracket on gr G; the p-power axiom gives the operator P of degree one, and P commutes with brackets (Schneider Proposition 25.1; ST03 §4, pp. 14–15).
Ordered bases exist for (G, ω) of finite rank (Schneider Proposition 26.6) and are characterised by the basis property of their symbols (Schneider Proposition 26.5).
acceptance: Computation, degenerate and non-example tests below pin the axioms and the saturation condition.

sources.locator: §23, Definition of a p-valuation, p. 169, and §26, Propositions 26.5–26.6, pp. 184–186
sources.match: Defines p-valuations with values above 1/(p−1), the filtration G_ν and graded Lie algebra gr G over 𝔽_p[P], finite rank, ordered bases and saturation.
Recalls Lazard's p-valuations, gr G over 𝔽_p[ε], ordered bases and the global chart, and states the hypothesis (HYP) used for the noncommutative Banach steps.

tests.name: not_pValuation_torsion
tests.statement: A p-valued group is torsion-free. If g ≠ 1 had order p, then ω(g^p) = ω(1) = ∞ would equal the finite value ω(g) + 1. If g ≠ 1 had finite order m prime to p, then g = (g^p)^k with pk ≡ 1 mod m, so ω(g) ≥ ω(g^p) = ω(g) + 1, again impossible. Hence ℤ/p is not p-valued, and neither is SL_2(ℤ_p) for any p, since −1 has order 2 (for p = 3 it also contains elements of order 3).

tests.name: not_isSaturated_shift
tests.statement: On the additive group ℤ_p (p odd), ω = v_p + 1 is a saturated p-valuation (ω(x) > p/(p−1) means v_p(x) ≥ 1, i.e. x ∈ pℤ_p is a p-th power), while ω = v_p + 2 is a p-valuation that is not saturated: the generator 1 has ω(1) = 2 > p/(p−1) but is not a p-th power.

nodes.title: Ordered bases give global coordinates
nodes.statement: Let (G, ω) be a p-valued group of finite rank d, complete for the topology defined by ω. Then (i) G is a pro-p group whose topology is defined by the subgroups G_ν, and it is topologically finitely generated; (ii) an ordered basis (h_1, …, h_d) exists; (iii) for every ordered basis the map ψ : ℤ_p^d → G, (x_1, …, x_d) ↦ h_1^{x_1} ⋯ h_d^{x_d}, is a homeomorphism satisfying ω(ψ(x)) = min_i (ω(h_i) + v_p(x_i)); (iv) the subgroups G^{p^n} generated by p^n-th powers are open, and for saturated (G, ω) they equal G_{ν+} for suitable ν.
hypotheses: Completeness and finite rank are both needed: an infinite product of copies of ℤ_p with ω = v_p is p-valued but not of finite rank, and has no finite ordered basis.
proofSteps: Finite rank makes every graded piece gr_ν G finite and puts the values of ω in finitely many progressions ν_j + ℕ_0 (Schneider §26, the discussion after Lemma 26.1, drawn there for a profinite G whose topology ω defines); so the filtration is countable and separated with finite p-group quotients G/G_ν, and completeness makes G = lim G/G_ν a pro-p group (Lazard II.1.1.5 as cited in ST03 p. 15).

An ordered basis is obtained by lifting an 𝔽_p[ε]-basis of gr G and ordering by ω (Schneider Proposition 26.6); Proposition 26.5 proves the equivalence of the basis condition and the ordered-product description.

The ordered-product map is continuous and bijective, by successive approximation along the filtration, and ω of an ordered product is the minimum of the ω(h_i^{x_i}) = ω(h_i) + v_p(x_i) (Schneider Proposition 26.5; ST03 p. 15 citing Lazard III.2.2.5/6). A continuous bijection from a compact space to a Hausdorff space is a homeomorphism.
The p-power subgroups are treated in Schneider Proposition 26.15 and Remark 26.9.
acceptance: For G = 1 + pℤ_p (p odd) with ω = v_p(· − 1) and ordered basis (1 + p), ψ(x) = (1 + p)^x and ω((1 + p)^x) = 1 + v_p(x).

sources.locator: §26, Lemma 26.1, Propositions 26.5, 26.6 and 26.15, pp. 181–191
sources.match: Proves that finite-rank p-valued groups have ordered bases, that ordered products give a bijective chart with the minimum formula for ω, and describes the p-power subgroups.
States that ψ : ℤ_p^d → G is a bijective global chart with ω(h^x) = min(ω(h_i) + ω_p(x_i)) and uses it to identify C(G, K) and C^an(G, K) with function spaces on ℤ_p^d.

nodes.title: Uniform pro-p groups are p-valued groups satisfying (HYP)
nodes.statement: Let p be odd and G a uniform pro-p group of dimension d (NoncommutativeAndEquivariantIwasawa NE.0). Define ω(1) = ∞ and ω(g) = n + 1 for g ∈ G^{p^n} ∖ G^{p^{n+1}}. Then ω is an integral p-valuation of rank d, every minimal topological generating set (g_1, …, g_d) is an ordered basis with ω(g_i) = 1, each element of G^{p} is a p-th power, and (G, ω, (g_i)) satisfies (HYP). Conversely, a compact group with a p-valuation and an ordered basis satisfying (HYP) is powerful and torsion-free, hence uniform. In particular ψ(x) = g_1^{x_1} ⋯ g_d^{x_d} is a homeomorphism ℤ_p^d → G and ω(ψ(x)) = 1 + min_i v_p(x_i).
hypotheses: p odd. For p = 2 the analogous statement replaces G by its Frattini subgroup (ST03 Theorem 5.1, step 1), and this roadmap does not use it.
proofSteps: The lower p-series of a uniform group is G^{p^n} and the p-power map induces bijections G^{p^n}/G^{p^{n+1}} → G^{p^{n+1}}/G^{p^{n+2}} (AW13 §10.2, recalling DDMS Lemma 4.10); this gives the three axioms of a p-valuation (AW13 §10.3, proof of the theorem, which cites Lazard II.2.1.2).
gr G ≅ ⊕ G^{p^n}/G^{p^{n+1}} is free of rank d over 𝔽_p[t] with basis the classes of a minimal generating set (AW13 Lemma 10.2), so these form an ordered basis with ω = 1.

Since ω(g_i) + ω(g_j) = 2 > p/(p−1) for p ≥ 3 and every element of G^p = {ω ≥ 2} is a p-th power, (HYP) holds (ST03 Remark after Lemma 4.3, p. 20). The converse is the same Remark: commutators of basis elements are p-th powers, so G is powerful, and a p-valued group is torsion-free.
The formula for ω on ordered products is ND.0/ordered-basis-chart.
acceptance: For G = 1 + pℤ_p ⊂ ℤ_p^× (p odd), which is uniform of dimension 1, ω(1 + p^n u) = n for a unit u, matching v_p(g − 1).

nodes.title: The analytic structure of a p-valued group
nodes.statement: (i) A p-valuable pro-p group G (one admitting a p-valuation of finite rank defining its topology) carries a unique structure of a locally ℚ_p-analytic manifold making it a p-adic Lie group, of dimension equal to its rank; for any ordered basis the chart ψ of ND.0/ordered-basis-chart is an analytic isomorphism ℤ_p^d → G, and the group operations are given in these coordinates by power series with coefficients in ℚ_p converging on ℤ_p^d. (ii) Conversely every p-adic Lie group G has a compact open subgroup G′ with an integral p-valuation defining its topology such that (G′, ω) is saturated and rank G′ = dim G; and every compact p-adic Lie group has an open normal subgroup which is uniform (for p odd) or p-valued satisfying (HYP).
hypotheses: Uniqueness is of the manifold structure compatible with the topology and the group operations; the chart ψ depends on the ordered basis, and two ordered bases give analytically compatible charts.
proofSteps: Schneider §29 shows that multiplication in ordered coordinates is given by power series (Proposition 29.2), hence that a p-valuable group is a p-adic Lie group (Corollary 29.6), uniquely so (Theorem 29.8).
Schneider Theorem 27.1 constructs, from a chart at the identity, a compact open subgroup with a saturated integral p-valuation of rank equal to the dimension.
An open normal uniform subgroup exists by ST03 §4, p. 14, citing DDMS Corollary 8.34; its p-valuation satisfies (HYP) by ND.0/uniform-groups-p-valued.
acceptance: For G = 1 + pℤ_p (p odd) the chart x ↦ (1 + p)^x = exp(x log(1 + p)) is analytic with analytic inverse x = log(g)/log(1 + p); the multiplication is (x, y) ↦ x + y.
For the first congruence subgroup of SL_2(ℤ_p) the analytic structure is the one induced from the ℚ_p-manifold SL_2(ℤ_p) (ND.0/first-congruence-sl2).

sources.match: Every p-adic Lie group has a compact open saturated p-valued subgroup of rank equal to its dimension; a p-valuable pro-p group has a unique p-adic Lie group structure, with multiplication analytic in ordered coordinates.

nodes.title: The Lazard Lie lattice and the Lie algebras g_R, g_K of a uniform group
nodes.statement: Let p be odd, G uniform of dimension d with minimal topological generating set (g_1, …, g_d), R a complete discrete valuation ring with fraction field K ⊇ ℚ_p. On the set G define λ·x = x^λ (λ ∈ ℤ_p), x + y = lim_{i→∞} (x^{p^i} y^{p^i})^{p^{−i}} and [x, y] = lim_{i→∞} (x^{−p^i} y^{−p^i} x^{p^i} y^{p^i})^{p^{−2i}}. These operations make G a Lie algebra L_G over ℤ_p, free of rank d with basis g_1, …, g_d, and powerful: [L_G, L_G] ⊆ p L_G. Put g_R := R ⊗_{ℤ_p} (1/p)L_G (an R-Lie algebra free of rank d, since [p⁻¹L_G, p⁻¹L_G] ⊆ p⁻¹L_G) and g_K := K ⊗_R g_R. The p-adic logarithm identifies L_G with a ℤ_p-lattice in the Lie algebra Lie(G) of the analytic group of ND.0/p-valued-analytic-structure, so g_{ℚ_p} = ℚ_p ⊗ L_G ≅ Lie(G), and L_{G^{p^n}} = p^n L_G.

nodes.title: The first congruence subgroup of SL₂(ℤ_p) and its Lie lattice
nodes.statement: (i) If G is a compact open uniform subgroup of SL_n(ℚ_p), its Lazard Lie algebra satisfies g_{ℚ_p} ≅ sl_n(ℚ_p), the isomorphism given by the matrix logarithm. (ii) Let p be odd and G_1 = ker(SL_2(ℤ_p) → SL_2(𝔽_p)). Then G_1 is uniform of dimension 3; with h = diag(1, −1), e = E_{12}, f = E_{21}, the elements exp(ph), exp(pe), exp(pf) form a minimal topological generating set; and (1/p)L_{G_1} = g_{ℤ_p} = ℤ_p h ⊕ ℤ_p e ⊕ ℤ_p f = sl_2(ℤ_p) with [h, e] = 2e, [h, f] = −2f, [e, f] = h. For G = G_1^m the corresponding statements hold componentwise, with g_{ℤ_p} = sl_2(ℤ_p)^m.
hypotheses: (i) is an identification of rational Lie algebras; the integral equality in (ii) is specific to the first congruence subgroup and p odd.
proofSteps: For x ∈ p M_2(ℤ_p) the exponential and logarithm series converge (p odd) and are mutually inverse bijections between p·sl_2(ℤ_p) and G_1; under them the commutator limits of ND.0/lazard-lie-lattice become the matrix bracket (Fu, proof of Lemma 5.6, citing DDMS Lemma 7.12). Hence L_{G_1} = p·sl_2(ℤ_p) and (1/p)L_{G_1} = sl_2(ℤ_p).

exp(px) for x ∈ {h, e, f} reduce to a basis of G_1/G_1^p ≅ sl_2(𝔽_p), so they are a minimal generating set, and G_1 is uniform since its lower p-series is G_1^{p^n} = ker(SL_2(ℤ_p) → SL_2(ℤ/p^{n+1})).

(i) is DDMS Chapter 9, Exercise 9, as cited by Fu Lemma 4.1: the matrix logarithm is a Lie algebra isomorphism from ℚ_p ⊗ L_G onto the Lie algebra of the closed subgroup G of SL_n(ℚ_p), which is sl_n(ℚ_p) since G is open.
acceptance: Under (ii), the Iwasawa algebra ℤ_p[[G_1]] is the noncommutative power series ring in F = exp(pf) − 1, H = exp(ph) − 1, E = exp(pe) − 1 (Fu p. 19).

The Casimir element Δ = ½h² − h + 2ef of U(sl_2) is four times the Killing-form Casimir of sl_2 (Tau Ceti's casimirElement): with κ(h, h) = 8 and κ(e, f) = 4 the dual basis of (h, e, f) is (h/8, f/4, e/4), giving h²/8 + (ef + fe)/4 = Δ/4.

nodes.title: The distribution algebra D(G, K) under convolution
nodes.statement: Let ℚ_p ⊆ L ⊆ K be complete fields with L/ℚ_p finite and K spherically complete (for instance discretely valued), and G a compact locally L-analytic group with multiplication m : G × G → G. D(G, K) := C^an(G, K)′_b is the nuclear Fréchet space of LocallyAnalyticDistributions:L0/locally-analytic-dual-nuclear, and its product is the convolution of LocallyAnalyticDistributions:L1/distribution-convolution: λ ∗ μ := m_*(λ ⊗ μ), using D(G × G, K) ≅ D(G, K) ⊗̂ D(G, K); explicitly (λ ∗ μ)(f) = λ(g ↦ μ(h ↦ f(gh))), which equals the iterated integral μ(h ↦ λ(g ↦ f(gh))) written there. That layer constructs the product, its associativity and its unit for K finite over ℚ_p and G compact ℚ_p-analytic; the same construction runs over L and any spherically complete K. In this generality (D(G, K), ∗) is an associative unital K-algebra with unit δ_1, convolution is jointly continuous, so D(G, K) is a Fréchet algebra; δ_g ∗ δ_h = δ_{gh}, so g ↦ δ_g is a group homomorphism G → D(G, K)^×; the induced map K[G] → D(G, K) is injective with dense image. D(G, K) is commutative iff G is.
hypotheses: The convolution product itself is owned by LocallyAnalyticDistributions:L1/distribution-convolution and is not constructed again; what this node adds is the generality (locally L-analytic G, spherically complete K), joint continuity and the Fréchet-algebra structure, the Dirac homomorphism with injectivity and density, functoriality and the commutativity criterion.
Compactness of G gives joint continuity; for a general locally analytic group D(G, K) is an algebra with separately continuous multiplication (ST02 Proposition 2.3), which this roadmap does not use.

The first factor is paired with the left variable of the product gh. Integrating in the other order gives the same element (Fubini, through D(G × G) ≅ D(G) ⊗̂ D(G)); pairing the first factor with the right variable instead gives the opposite algebra, which the tests distinguish.
proofSteps: The external product C^an(G) ⊗̂ C^an(G) ≅ C^an(G × G) (LocallyAnalyticDistributions:L0/locally-analytic-product) dualises to D(G × G) ≅ D(G) ⊗̂ D(G) (LocallyAnalyticDistributions:L0/locally-analytic-dual-nuclear), and m_* = (m^*)′ is continuous (LocallyAnalyticDistributions:L0/locally-analytic-pullback). The composite is the convolution of ST02 §2, p. 8, and for K finite over ℚ_p and L = ℚ_p it is LocallyAnalyticDistributions:L1/distribution-convolution; the stagewise construction there runs unchanged over L and any spherically complete K.

Associativity and the unit are part of LocallyAnalyticDistributions:L1/distribution-convolution; in the general setting they follow on Dirac distributions from associativity of m and extend by continuity and density of the span of Dirac distributions (ST02 Proposition 2.3, p. 9, and Lemma 3.1, p. 13).

Injectivity of K[G] → D(G, K): distinct points are separated by locally constant, hence locally analytic, functions. Density: a continuous linear form on D(G, K) vanishing on all δ_g is, by reflexivity, a locally analytic function vanishing everywhere (ST02 Lemma 3.1 and its proof).
acceptance: For G = ℤ_p (additive, L = ℚ_p) D(G, K) is the commutative algebra of LocallyAnalyticDistributions:L0/locally-analytic-distributions, and the Amice transform carries convolution to multiplication of power series on the open disc (LocallyAnalyticDistributions L1).

nodes.title: The enveloping algebra inside D(G, K)
nodes.statement: Let G be a compact locally L-analytic group with Lie algebra g (over L). For x ∈ g let x̃ ∈ D(G, K) be the distribution f ↦ (d/dt) f(exp(tx))|_{t=0}. The map x ↦ x̃ is L-linear and satisfies x̃ ∗ ỹ − ỹ ∗ x̃ = [x, y]~, so it extends to a K-algebra homomorphism U(g) ⊗_L K = U(g_K) → D(G, K), which is injective. For λ ∈ D(G, K), x̃ ∗ λ = lim_{t→0} t⁻¹(δ_{exp(tx)} − δ_1) ∗ λ in D(G, K). For g ∈ G, δ_g ∗ x̃ ∗ δ_{g⁻¹} = (Ad(g)x)~. Under the action of D(G, K) on C^an(G, K) by the contragredient of left translation, x̃ acts by the derivation f ↦ (d/dt) f(exp(−tx)·)|_{t=0}.
hypotheses: The sign is fixed by x̃(f) = (d/dt) f(exp(tx))|₀ on the identity; Fu writes the Lie action on functions by (22) with t·x the ℤ_p-scaling of the Lazard lattice, which is the same distribution for x ∈ g_{ℤ_p}.
proofSteps: x̃ = x·δ_1 for the derivative action of g on distributions (ST02 §2, p. 12), and the limit formula holds in C^an(G, K)′_s, hence in D(G, K) because bounded sets of the reflexive space are contained in c-compact ones on which the weak and strong topologies agree (ST02 p. 12).

The commutator relation follows from the limit formula and the Campbell–Hausdorff expansion exp(tx)exp(sy)exp(−tx)exp(−sy) = exp(ts[x, y] + O(t²s, ts²)); the universal property of U(g) (Mathlib UniversalEnvelopingAlgebra.lift) gives the algebra map.

Injectivity: pairing with polynomial functions in a chart at 1 computes the PBW coefficients (the distributions supported at 1 are dual to germs of analytic functions, and the monomials x^α pair nondegenerately with coordinate monomials), using the PBW basis theorem of LieHighestWeight Layer 3.
Conjugation: δ_g ∗ x̃ ∗ δ_{g⁻¹}(f) = (d/dt) f(g exp(tx) g⁻¹)|₀ = (Ad(g)x)~(f) (Fu, proof of Proposition 5.3, p. 17, in the language of functions).
acceptance: For G = ℤ_p and x = 1 ∈ Lie(ℤ_p) = ℚ_p, x̃(f) = f′(0); its Amice transform is log(1 + T) (LocallyAnalyticDistributions convention 5).

nodes.title: The rational Iwasawa algebra K[[G]] inside D(G, K)
nodes.statement: Let G be a compact locally ℚ_p-analytic group, o_L the integers of a finite extension L ⊆ K. Let o_L[[G]] = lim_N o_L[G/N] (N open normal) be the completed group ring of PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras L1 (the integral measures on G), and L[[G]] := L ⊗_{o_L} o_L[[G]] (the bounded L-valued measures). Restricting a measure to locally analytic test functions defines an injective continuous K-algebra-compatible map L[[G]] → D(G, K), extending g ↦ δ_g; its image is dense. When (G, ω) is p-valued with an ordered basis h_1, …, h_d and b_i = h_i − 1, b^α = b_1^{α_1} ⋯ b_d^{α_d} (ordered product), every λ ∈ D(G, K) has a unique convergent expansion λ = Σ_α d_α b^α with d_α ∈ K and sup_α |d_α| r^{τ_α} < ∞ for every 0 < r < 1, where τ_α = Σ_i α_i ω(h_i); conversely every such series converges in D(G, K). The coefficient d_α is the α-th Mahler coefficient pairing: b^α(f) = c_α(ψ^*f), so d_α is determined by λ on the Mahler basis binom(x, α) in the coordinates ψ. A distribution lies in ℤ_p[[G]] iff all d_α ∈ ℤ_p, and in L[[G]] iff the d_α lie in L and are bounded.
hypotheses: The coefficient description uses the chart ψ of ND.0/ordered-basis-chart; it depends on the ordered basis, but the norms built from it do not (ND.2/banach-steps).
L[[G]] is not lim_N L[G/N]: bounded measures are o_L[[G]][1/p] (PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras L1).
proofSteps: Bounded measures are continuous linear forms on C(G, L); restriction to C^an(G, K) is continuous and injective because locally constant functions are dense in C(G, L) and are locally analytic (LocallyAnalyticDistributions:L0/locally-analytic-function-space). Multiplicativity holds on Dirac measures and extends by density and continuity.

The finite-difference computation gives b^α(f) = c_α(ψ^*f). Duality then gives the coefficient description of distributions (ST03 pp. 16–17).

nodes.title: Finite free decomposition over an open subgroup
nodes.statement: Let G be a compact locally L-analytic group and H ⊆ G an open subgroup with coset representatives g_1 = 1, …, g_l of G/H. Then D(G, K) = ⊕_{i} δ_{g_i} ∗ D(H, K) = ⊕_i D(H, K) ∗ δ_{g_i}: D(G, K) is a free left and right D(H, K)-module of rank [G : H] with basis the δ_{g_i}, and the decomposition is topological (D(G, K) ≅ D(H, K)^l). If H is normal, conjugation by δ_g preserves D(H, K) and D(G, K) is the crossed product D(H, K) ∗ (G/H) in the sense of McConnell–Robson §1.5.8: a free D(H, K)-module on units ḡ, ḡ ∈ G/H, with ḡ D(H, K) = D(H, K) ḡ and ḡ h̄ ∈ D(H, K)^× · (gh)‾.
proofSteps: G is the disjoint union of the open cosets g_iH, so C^an(G, K) = Π_i C^an(g_iH, K) topologically (LocallyAnalyticDistributions:L0/locally-analytic-function-space), and translation by g_i identifies C^an(g_iH, K) with C^an(H, K); dualising gives the decomposition (ST02 proof of Lemma 3.1, p. 13; ST03 Theorem 5.1, step 1, p. 29).

For normal H, δ_g ∗ D(H, K) ∗ δ_{g⁻¹} = D(H, K) because conjugation by g is an analytic automorphism of H; the crossed product axioms follow with twisting δ_{g_i} δ_{g_j} = δ_{h_{ij}} δ_{g_k}, h_{ij} ∈ H.
acceptance: For G = ℤ_p and H = pℤ_p, D(ℤ_p, K) = ⊕_{a=0}^{p−1} δ_a ∗ D(pℤ_p, K); under the Amice transform this is the decomposition of power series by residue classes.

nodes.title: The centre of U(g) is central in D(G, K)
nodes.statement: Let G be an open (compact) subgroup of the group G(L) of L-rational points of a connected linear algebraic group G over L, with Lie algebra g. Then the image of Z(g) ⊗_L K under U(g_K) → D(G, K) lies in the centre of D(G, K). Consequently, for every g ∈ G and z ∈ Z(g), z commutes with δ_g, and z acts on C^an(G, K) by G-equivariant continuous endomorphisms for both the left and the right translation action.
hypotheses: Connectedness of G is essential: for a disconnected group the adjoint action of G(L) on U(g) need not fix Z(g) (for G = O(2), where U(so(2)) = Z(so(2)) = K[x], an element of determinant −1 sends x to −x, so x is not central in D(O(2)(L) ∩ GL_2(o_L), K)).
proofSteps: By density of Dirac distributions (ND.1/distribution-algebra) it suffices to show δ_g ∗ z ∗ δ_{g⁻¹} = z, i.e. that the adjoint action of G(L) on U(g) fixes Z(g); by ND.1/lie-algebra-in-distributions δ_g ∗ x̃ ∗ δ_{g⁻¹} = (Ad(g)x)~ on generators.
For connected G the adjoint action of G(L) fixes Z(g) (ST02 Proposition 3.7, p. 16, citing Bourbaki and Demazure–Gabriel II §6.1.5); the equivariance on functions follows by transposition.
acceptance: For G = G_1 ⊂ SL_2(ℤ_p) (p odd) the Casimir Δ = ½h² − h + 2ef is central in D(G_1, ℚ_p).

nodes.title: Fréchet–Stein algebras
nodes.statement: Let K be a complete nonarchimedean field. A K-Fréchet algebra is an associative unital K-algebra A with a Fréchet topology for which multiplication is continuous. For a continuous seminorm q on A let A_q be the completion of A/{q = 0}; q is an algebra seminorm if q(ab) ≤ c q(a) q(b) for some c > 0, and then A_q is a K-Banach algebra and A → A_q an algebra map with dense image. A is a (left) K-Fréchet–Stein algebra if there is an increasing sequence q_1 ≤ q_2 ≤ … of continuous algebra seminorms defining the topology such that, for every n, (i) A_{q_n} is left noetherian, and (ii) A_{q_n} is flat as a right A_{q_{n+1}}-module via the transition map. Then A ≅ lim_n A_{q_n} as Fréchet algebras.
hypotheses: Flatness is on the side that makes A_{q_n} ⊗_{A_{q_{n+1}}} (−) exact on left modules; two-sided Fréchet–Stein means both one-sided conditions.
proofSteps: The limit isomorphism holds for any defining increasing sequence of seminorms, and algebra seminorms make the transitions algebra maps (ST03 §3, pp. 7–8).
acceptance: A K-Banach algebra that is left noetherian is Fréchet–Stein with the constant sequence; the tests below exhibit the nondegenerate case.

nodes.title: Coherent sheaves and coadmissible modules
nodes.statement: Let A be a K-Fréchet–Stein algebra with defining sequence (q_n). A coherent sheaf for (A, (q_n)) is a family (M_n)_n of finitely generated left A_{q_n}-modules with A_{q_n}-linear isomorphisms A_{q_n} ⊗_{A_{q_{n+1}}} M_{n+1} ≅ M_n; morphisms are compatible families. Its global sections are Γ(M_n) := lim_n M_n, a left A-module. A left A-module is coadmissible if it is isomorphic to Γ(M_n) for some coherent sheaf. The full subcategory 𝒞_A of Mod(A) of coadmissible modules does not depend on the defining sequence. A coadmissible module carries its canonical topology, the projective limit of the canonical Banach topologies of the finitely generated A_{q_n}-modules M_n; it is a K-Fréchet space with continuous A-action.
hypotheses: Left modules throughout. The transition isomorphisms are A_{q_n} ⊗_{A_{q_{n+1}}} M_{n+1} ≅ M_n with the Banach algebra on the left; BCGP Definition 2.2.31 writes the tensor factors in the opposite order (recorded under sourceIssues).
proofSteps: Independence of the sequence is a cofinality argument (ST03 p. 8). The canonical topology on a finitely generated module over a noetherian Banach algebra is the quotient topology from any finite free presentation (ST03 Proposition 2.1, p. 6).
acceptance: Finitely presented A-modules are coadmissible (ND.2/coadmissible-theorems); A itself corresponds to the coherent sheaf (A_{q_n}).

nodes.title: Theorems A and B and the abelian category of coadmissible modules
nodes.statement: Let A be a K-Fréchet–Stein algebra, (M_n) a coherent sheaf and M = Γ(M_n). (A) For every n the map M → M_n has dense image for the canonical topology. (B) lim^{(i)}_n M_n = 0 for all i ≥ 1; hence Γ is exact. Consequences: A_{q_n} ⊗_A M ≅ M_n for every n; A_{q_n} is flat as a right A-module; Γ : Coh(A, (q_n)) → 𝒞_A is an equivalence; 𝒞_A is an abelian subcategory of Mod(A), closed under finite direct sums, kernels, cokernels, images, sums of coadmissible submodules and finitely generated submodules; finitely presented A-modules are coadmissible. For a submodule N of a coadmissible M: N is coadmissible ⇔ M/N is coadmissible ⇔ N is closed in the canonical topology. Every A-linear map between coadmissible modules is continuous and strict; every finitely generated left ideal of A is closed. If I ⊆ A is a closed two-sided ideal, A/I is a K-Fréchet–Stein algebra with defining completions A_{q_n}/A_{q_n}I and A/I ≅ lim_n A_{q_n}/A_{q_n}I. If A → B is a continuous algebra map of Fréchet–Stein algebras with B coadmissible over A, a B-module is coadmissible over B iff over A.
proofSteps: (A): for m > n choose a surjection A_{q_m}^r → M_m; the image of A_{q_m}^r in A_{q_n}^r is dense, and all maps are continuous for canonical topologies (ST03 Proposition 2.1.iii), so M_m → M_n has dense image; conclude by the Mittag-Leffler argument of Bourbaki (ST03 p. 9).
(B) follows from (A) by EGA III 0.13.2.4 (ST03 p. 9). Corollaries 3.1, 3.3, 3.4 and 3.5 and Remark 3.2 are formal consequences (ST03 pp. 9–11).

Closed ⇔ coadmissible: the closure of N is Γ(N_n) for the images N_n ⊆ M_n (ST03 Lemma 3.6). Continuity and strictness use the open mapping theorem for Fréchet spaces (LocallyAnalyticDistributions:L0/banach-open-mapping-lifts).
Quotients by closed two-sided ideals: ST03 Proposition 3.7, using flat base change for the transitions; restriction along A → B: ST03 Lemma 3.8.

nodes.title: The norms ‖·‖_r and the Banach steps D_r(G, K)
nodes.statement: Let K ⊆ ℂ_p be complete and discretely valued, |p| = 1/p, and let (G, ω) be a compact p-valued group with rational-valued ω and ordered basis (h_1, …, h_d), b_i = h_i − 1, τ_α = Σ α_i ω(h_i). For 1/p ≤ r < 1 and λ = Σ d_α b^α ∈ D(G, K) put ‖λ‖_r := sup_α |d_α| r^{τ_α}. Then ‖·‖_r is a norm on D(G, K), submultiplicative for 1/p ≤ r < 1, independent of the ordered basis (for fixed ω), the family (‖·‖_r)_{1/p≤r<1} defines the Fréchet topology, and ‖δ_g‖_r = 1. D_r(G, K) is the completion: the K-Banach algebra of all series Σ d_α b^α with |d_α| r^{τ_α} → 0 as |α| → ∞. The larger space D_{<r}(G, K) of series with sup_α |d_α| r^{τ_α} < ∞ (bounded, not tending to zero) is distinct from D_r(G, K); for r′ < r one has D_r ⊆ D_{<r} ⊆ D_{r′}, so lim_r D_r = lim_r D_{<r} = D(G, K) although at a fixed radius the two differ. When G is uniform with the integral p-valuation of ND.0/uniform-groups-p-valued, τ_α = |α| and ‖λ‖_r = sup |d_α| r^{|α|}, which is Fu's norm.
hypotheses: Submultiplicativity needs r ≥ 1/p (ST03 Lemma 4.1.ii); below 1/p the expansions of b_βb_γ have coefficients that can increase the norm.
Fu's display (16) describes D_r by bounded coefficients; that is D_{<r}, not the completion (sourceIssues).
proofSteps: The structure constants b_βb_γ = Σ c_{βγ,α} b^α lie in ℤ_p with v_p(c_{βγ,α}) ≥ τ_β + τ_γ − τ_α, because ‖·‖_{1/p} is multiplicative on ℤ_p[[G]] (Lazard III.2.3, cited in ST03 p. 17); hence |c_{βγ,α}| r^{τ_α} ≤ r^{τ_β+τ_γ} for 1/p ≤ r ≤ 1 (ST03 Lemma 4.1) and ‖λμ‖_r ≤ ‖λ‖_r‖μ‖_r (ST03 Proposition 4.2).
The completion is described by the c₀ condition because finite sums are dense for ‖·‖_r and the coefficient functionals are continuous (ST03 p. 18).
Independence of the ordered basis: expanding one basis in the other, v_p(c_{β,α}) ≥ max(0, τ′_β − τ_α), which gives the two inequalities of norms (ST03 p. 25).
D_r ⊆ D_{<r} is trivial; D_{<r} ⊆ D_{r′} for r′ < r because |d_α| r′^{τ_α} = |d_α| r^{τ_α}(r′/r)^{τ_α} → 0. The example of the tests shows D_r ≠ D_{<r}.
acceptance: For G = ℤ_p (uniform of dimension 1), ‖Σ d_n T^n‖_r = sup |d_n| r^n with T = δ_1 − 1: D_r(ℤ_p, K) is the ring of power series in T converging on the closed disc |T| ≤ r (up to the Amice normalisation), and D(ℤ_p, K) = lim_r D_r the functions on the open disc.

nodes.title: Graded rings, multiplicativity and noetherianity of D_r(G, K)
nodes.statement: Assume (HYP) for (G, ω, (h_i)) and K discretely valued with residue field k and gr·K ≅ k[ε_o, ε_o^{−1}]. Let 1/p < r < 1. (i) The associated graded ring of D_r(G, K) for the filtration F^s_r = {‖·‖_r ≤ p^{−s}} is gr·K ⊗_{𝔽_p[ε]} gr·_r ℤ_p[[G]], a commutative polynomial ring over gr·K in the principal symbols σ_r(b_1), …, σ_r(b_d); the same holds for ℤ_p[[G]] over 𝔽_p[ε] and for K[[G]]. Hence ‖·‖_r is multiplicative and D_r(G, K) has no zero divisors. (ii) If moreover r ∈ p^ℚ, then D_r(G, K) and ℤ_p[[G]] are left and right noetherian integral domains. (iii) At r = 1/p, ℤ_p[[G]], L[[G]] and D_{1/p}(G, K) are left and right noetherian integral domains with multiplicative norm ‖·‖_{1/p}, and gr·_{1/p} ℤ_p[[G]] ≅ U(gr G), the enveloping algebra of the 𝔽_p[ε]-Lie algebra gr G, which need not be commutative.
hypotheses: Noetherianity at real radii r ∉ p^ℚ is not asserted: the proof uses that the filtration is quasi-integral, which needs r ∈ p^ℚ and rational ω. Fu Theorem 4.2 states noetherianity for all 1/p ≤ r < 1 (sourceIssues).
The commutativity of the graded ring in (i) uses (HYP) through ST03 Lemma 4.4; at r = 1/p the graded ring is U(gr G), commutative only when gr G is abelian.
proofSteps: gr·_r ℤ_p[[G]] is free over 𝔽_p[ε] on the symbols σ_r(b^α) = Π σ_r(b_i)^{α_i}; base change to gr·K and to the completion is ST03 Lemma 4.3.

The symbols commute: under (HYP), h_i^{−1}h_j^{−1}h_ih_j = g^p and b_ib_j − b_jb_i = h_jh_i(g^p − 1) has ‖·‖_r < ‖b_ib_j‖_r for 1/p < r (ST03 Lemma 4.4). A filtered ring whose graded ring is a domain has multiplicative norm (ST03 Theorem 4.5.i).

Noetherianity for r ∈ p^ℚ: the filtration is quasi-integral and complete with noetherian graded ring, so ST03 Proposition 1.1 (Zariskian filtrations; NoncommutativeAndEquivariantIwasawa:NE.0/zariskian-noetherian) applies (ST03 Theorem 4.5.ii).
r = 1/p: Lazard's theorem gr·_{1/p} ℤ_p[[G]] ≅ U(gr G) (Lazard III.2.3.3, cited ST03 p. 17; Schneider Theorem 28.3) is a noetherian domain, and Proposition 1.1 gives (iii) (ST03 Remark 4.6).
acceptance: For G = ℤ_p and r ∈ (1/p, 1), gr·_r D_r(ℤ_p, K) = gr·K[σ(T)], the Gauss-norm graded ring of a closed-disc algebra.
For G = G_1 ⊂ SL_2(ℤ_p) (p odd) and 1/p < r < 1, gr·_r D_r(G_1, ℚ_p) ≅ 𝔽_p[ε, ε^{−1}][F, H, E] (Fu, proof of Theorem 5.7).

nodes.title: D(G, K) is a Fréchet–Stein algebra
nodes.statement: (i) Assume (HYP) and K discretely valued. For 1/p < r′ ≤ r < 1 in p^ℚ the transition D_r(G, K) → D_{r′}(G, K) is flat (on both sides), through D_r → D_{<r} → D_{r′}; hence D(G, K) is a two-sided K-Fréchet–Stein algebra for the norms ‖·‖_r, r ∈ p^ℚ ∩ (1/p, 1), for instance r_n = p^{−1/p^n}. (ii) For an arbitrary compact locally L-analytic group G (L/ℚ_p finite, K discretely valued), D(G, K) is a two-sided K-Fréchet–Stein algebra: choose an open normal uniform subgroup H_0 of the underlying ℚ_p-analytic group G_0 (p odd; for p = 2 its Frattini subgroup), with the conjugation-invariant p-valuation from the lower p-series, put q_r(Σ_i λ_i δ_{g_i}) = max_i ‖λ_i‖_r on D(G_0, K) = ⊕ D(H_0, K)δ_{g_i}, and pass to the quotient D(G_0, K) → D(G, K).
proofSteps: Flatness of D_r → D_{<r}: after a finite extension of K making r^{ω(h_i)} = |π|^{m_i/e}, the graded ring of F^0_r D_{<r} is k[[u_1, …, u_d]] and that of D_r is k[u_1, …, u_d]; polynomial → power series is flat, and ST03 Proposition 1.2 lifts graded flatness (ST03 Lemma 4.8).
Flatness of D_{<r} → D_{r′}: the graded map is a localisation in ε_o (ST03 Theorem 4.9, pp. 23–24). With ND.2/banach-step-structure (ii) this gives (i) (ST03 Theorem 4.10).

General G: conjugation preserves the lower p-series, so ‖δ_g λ δ_{g⁻¹}‖_r = ‖λ‖_r by basis independence; q_r is submultiplicative up to the constant max ‖λ_k(δ_{g_ig_j})‖_r, D_r(G_0, K) is free of rank l over D_r(H_0, K), hence noetherian, and flatness follows by base change (ST03 Theorem 5.1, step 1). Step 2 passes from G_0 to the L-analytic G by the closed quotient map D(G_0, K) → D(G, K) and ST03 Proposition 3.7 (ND.2/coadmissible-theorems).
acceptance: For G = ℤ_p, (i) is the Fréchet–Stein structure of the functions on the open unit disc.
For G = G_1^m ⊂ SL_2(ℤ_p)^m (p odd), D(G, ℚ_p) is Fréchet–Stein for the radii r_n = p^{−1/p^n}, which are the radii of Fu Proposition 5.3.

nodes.title: Faithful flatness of D(G, K) over the Iwasawa algebra
nodes.statement: Let L ⊆ K be finite over ℚ_p, K discretely valued. (i) Under (HYP), the maps ℤ_p[[G]] → L[[G]] → D_r(G, K) are flat (both sides) for every 1/p ≤ r < 1 with r ∈ p^ℚ. (ii) Under (HYP), L[[G]] → D(G, K) is faithfully flat: D(G, K) is faithfully flat as a left and as a right L[[G]]-module. (iii) For an arbitrary compact locally ℚ_p-analytic group G_0, L[[G_0]] → D(G_0, K) is faithfully flat. In particular, for K finite over ℚ_p (taking L = K) and a finitely generated K[[G]]-module M, D(G, K) ⊗_{K[[G]]} M = 0 implies M = 0, and the functor is exact.
hypotheses: Flatness of D_r over ℤ_p[[G]] uses the graded criterion ST03 Proposition 1.2 and r ∈ p^ℚ (or r = 1/p via Remark 4.6).
proofSteps: (i): the graded map is a base extension of 𝔽_p[ε] → gr·K, which is flat; ST03 Proposition 1.2 and Theorem 4.5.i lift this to the filtered rings; the trace L → ℚ_p makes D_r ⊗_{L[[G]]} M a direct summand of D_r ⊗_{ℤ_p[[G]]} M (ST03 Proposition 4.7).

(ii) flatness: for a left ideal J of the noetherian ring L[[G]], D ⊗ J is finitely presented hence coadmissible, so D ⊗ J = lim_r D_r ⊗ J and injectivity follows from (i) and left exactness of lim (ST03 Theorem 4.11, pp. 25–26).

(ii) faithfulness: reduce to a proper left ideal J ⊆ o[[G]] with o[[G]]/J p-torsion-free and show D_r J ≠ D_r for some r, comparing the graded modules of D_r/D_rJ and o[[G]]/J (ST03 pp. 26–28, with Lemma 4.12).
(iii) passes to an open normal subgroup with (HYP) by ND.1/open-subgroup-decomposition (ST03 Theorem 5.2, p. 30).
acceptance: For G = ℤ_p, ℚ_p[[T]]-modules ℚ_p ⊗ ℤ_p[[T]]/(f) with f distinguished survive in D(ℤ_p, ℚ_p): the zeros of f lie in the open unit disc.

nodes.title: The p-adically completed enveloping algebra Û(h)_K
nodes.statement: Let R be a complete discrete valuation ring with uniformiser π and fraction field K, and h an R-Lie algebra which is free of finite rank as an R-module, with R-basis u_1, …, u_d. The π-adic completion Û(h) := lim_a U(h)/π^a U(h) is an R-lattice in the K-Banach algebra Û(h)_K := Û(h) ⊗_R K, whose norm has unit ball Û(h). By the PBW theorem every element of Û(h)_K is uniquely a convergent sum Σ_α c_α u^α (ordered monomials, c_α ∈ K, c_α → 0), and ‖Σ c_α u^α‖ = sup |c_α|. For n ≥ 0 put Û(h)_{n,K} := Û(π^n h)_K (the n-th deformation). Each Û(h)_{n,K} is a left and right noetherian K-Banach algebra (an almost commutative affinoid algebra in the sense of AW13 §3.8) with Gr(Û(h)_{n,K}) ≅ gr U(h)/π gr U(h) ≅ Sym(h ⊗ k); the inclusions U(h_K) ⊂ Û(h)_{n+1,K} ⊂ Û(h)_{n,K} are dense. For a finite extension K′/K with integers R′ and ramification index e, K′ ⊗_K Û(h)_{n,K} ≅ Û(R′ ⊗_R h)_{en,K′}; in particular Û(R′ ⊗_R h)_{K′} ≅ K′ ⊗_K Û(h)_K.
hypotheses: h must be free of finite rank over R; for the Lie algebras of uniform groups this holds with h = g_R = (1/p) R L_G (ND.0/lazard-lie-lattice).
The base change statement is for finite extensions K′/K, as used for coefficient extension in ND.4/microlocal-coefficient-extension and ND.5/central-injectivity-theorem.
proofSteps: U(h) is a deformable R-algebra (AW13 Example 3.4(c)) because gr U(h) ≅ Sym(h) is flat over R; the π-adic completion of a deformable algebra is a complete doubly filtered K-algebra with Gr ≅ gr A/π gr A (AW13 §3.7, Lemma and Corollary).
Noetherianity: an almost commutative affinoid algebra is noetherian by Li–Van Oystaeyen II.2.2.1 (AW13 §3.8, Proposition and the remark before it).

PBW description: the ordered monomials u^α span U(h) over R (the spanning half of PBW at the pinned Tau Ceti, TauCeti.UniversalEnvelopingAlgebra.span_orderedPBWMonomials_eq_pbwFiltration, valid over any commutative ring) and are R-linearly independent because their images in U(h_K) are (the PBW basis theorem over the field K, LieHighestWeight Layer 3); so they form an R-basis of U(h) and gr U(h) ≅ Sym(h); π-adic completion turns finite sums into null sequences.
Base change: AW13 Lemma 3.9(c), which needs [K′ : K] < ∞ and multiplies the deformation index by e.
acceptance: For h = R·u abelian of rank one, Û(h)_K = K⟨u⟩ is the Tate algebra in one variable, and Û(π^n h)_K = K⟨π^n u⟩ is the Tate algebra of the disc of radius |π|^{−n}.

nodes.title: The closure U_r(g, K) of U(g) in D_r(G, K)
nodes.statement: Let G be uniform (p odd) with ordered basis g_1, …, g_d, b_i = g_i − 1, and let x_i := log(1 + b_i) = Σ_{n≥1} (−1)^{n+1} b_i^n / n, the image in D(G, K) of log(g_i) ∈ g = L_G ⊗ ℚ_p. For 0 < r < 1, U_r(g, K) is the closure of the image of U(g_K) (ND.1/lie-algebra-in-distributions) in the Banach algebra D_r(G, K). It is a closed subalgebra, stable under conjugation by the δ_g, g ∈ G, and for r′ ≤ r the transition D_r → D_{r′} maps U_r(g, K) into U_{r′}(g, K).
proofSteps: Closure of a subalgebra in a Banach algebra is a subalgebra. Stability under conjugation follows from δ_g x̃ δ_{g⁻¹} = (Ad(g)x)~ (ND.1/lie-algebra-in-distributions) and continuity of conjugation (Fu, proof of Proposition 5.3, p. 17).

x_i is the image of log(g_i) because the logarithm series converges in D_r(G, K) for r < 1 and computes the derivative of t ↦ δ_{g_i^t} at t = 0 (Kohlhaase §1.4, where X = (log(1 + b_i))_i is the basis of g used).
acceptance: For G = ℤ_p and r ∈ (p^{−1}, 1), U_r(Lie ℤ_p, K) is the closure of K[x] with x = log(1 + T): the power series in log(1 + T) converging for the norm ‖·‖_r (Frommer's theorem below).

nodes.title: Frommer's description of D_r(G, K) over U_r(g, K)
nodes.statement: Let K be discretely valued, G a uniform pro-p group (more generally a p-valued group as in Kohlhaase §1.4, with τ_i = ω(h_i)), r ∈ p^ℚ with 1/p < r < 1, and x_i = log(1 + b_i). Then: (i) U_r(g, K) = {Σ_α d_α x^α : d_α ∈ K, |d_α| ‖x^α‖_r → 0}, with ‖Σ d_α x^α‖_r = sup_α |d_α| ‖x^α‖_r; (ii) U_r(g, K) is a noetherian subalgebra of D_r(G, K); (iii) there are integers ℓ_i ≥ 1, ℓ_i = max{m ≥ 1 : sup_{n≥1} |1/n| r^{nτ_i} = |1/m| r^{mτ_i}}, such that D_r(G, K) is a free right U_r(g, K)-module with basis the b^α, 0 ≤ α_i < ℓ_i. For a closed uniform subgroup H compatible with G the same holds for D(H, K), and the closure of D(G, K)·D(H, K) in D_r(G, K) is a finitely generated free U_r(g, K)-module with basis in K[H].
hypotheses: r must lie in p^ℚ ∩ (1/p, 1); the source states the theorem only there. Frommer's original proof (Münster SFB 478 preprint 265, 2003) was not available; the statement is taken from Kohlhaase's summary and his proof of Corollary 1.4.1.
proofSteps: The orthogonality of the monomials x^α for ‖·‖_r is shown by a careful analysis of orthogonal bases (Frommer §1.4, Lemma 3 and Corollaries 1–3, as cited by Kohlhaase).
The integers ℓ_i record where the maximum in ‖log(1 + b_i)‖_r = max_n |1/n| r^{nτ_i} is attained; the b^α with α_i < ℓ_i fill the remaining coordinates (Kohlhaase, proof of Corollary 1.4.1).
Noetherianity of U_r(g, K) follows from its graded ring being a polynomial ring, as for D_r (ND.2/banach-step-structure).
acceptance: For G uniform with τ_i = 1 and r = r_n = p^{−1/p^n}, the maximum max_k r_n^{p^k}/|p^k| is attained exactly at k = n, so ℓ_i = p^n and ‖x_i‖_{r_n} = p^{n−1}: D_{r_n} is free over U_{r_n} on the b^α with α_i < p^n, which matches the coset count [G : G^{p^n}] = p^{nd} (Fu Proposition 5.3).

sources.locator: §1.4, Theorem (Frommer) and Corollary 1.4.1 with proof, pp. 15–16
sources.match: Summarises Frommer's theorem: for r ∈ p^ℚ, 1/p < r < 1, U_r(g, K) is a noetherian subalgebra described by weighted series in x_i = log(1 + b_i), and D_r(G_0, K) is free over it with basis the b^α, α_i < ℓ_i; extends this to compatible uniform subgroups.

nodes.title: D_{r_n}(G, ℚ_p) as a crossed product of U_{r_n}(g) by G/G^{p^n}
nodes.statement: Let p be odd, G uniform with minimal generators g_i, ω(g_i) = 1, and r_n = p^{−1/p^n} for n ≥ 1. Then (i) ‖log(1 + b_i)‖_{r_n} = p^{n−1}; (ii) for every g ∈ G, g^{p^n} ∈ U_{r_n}(g), since g^{p^n} = exp(p^n log g) and the exponential series converges in U_{r_n}(g); (iii) D_{r_n}(G, ℚ_p) is a crossed product U_{r_n}(g) ∗ (G/G^{p^n}): it is a free left and right U_{r_n}(g)-module on δ_γ for any set of coset representatives γ of G/G^{p^n}, with δ_γ U_{r_n}(g) = U_{r_n}(g) δ_γ and twisting in U_{r_n}(g)^× ∩ δ_{G^{p^n}}; (iv) if G is open in the ℚ_p-points of a connected split reductive group, then for every character λ of Z(g), D^λ_{r_n}(G, ℚ_p) ≅ U^λ_{r_n}(g) ∗ (G/G^{p^n}).
hypotheses: The crossed product is not a tensor product with the group algebra of G/G^{p^n}: the twisting cocycle is nontrivial whenever G/G^{p^n} does not lift to a subgroup.
proofSteps: (i): ‖log(1 + b_i)‖_r = max_k r^{p^k}/|p^k| = max_k p^{k − p^{k−n}}, which equals p^{n−1} at k = n and is strictly smaller for every other k ≥ 0 (k − p^{k−n} < n − 1 for k ≠ n when p ≥ 3) (Fu, proof of Proposition 5.3, p. 17).

(ii): ‖x_i^k‖_{r_n} = p^{(n−1)k} by multiplicativity (ND.2/banach-step-structure) and |p^{nk}/k!| p^{(n−1)k} ≤ p^{k/(p−1)} p^{−k} → 0, so exp(p^n x_i) converges in U_{r_n}(g), and it equals g_i^{p^n}; products of such elements give all of G^{p^n} by ordered coordinates.

(iii): Frommer's freeness (ND.3/frommer-theorem) with ℓ_i = p^n, the elements b^α, α_i < p^n, span the same right U_{r_n}-module as the δ_γ for coset representatives; U_{r_n} is stable under conjugation (ND.3/radius-enveloping-closure).
(iv): Z(g) is central in D_r (ND.1/central-enveloping-distributions) and contained in U_{r_n}(g), so the crossed-product structure passes to the quotient by the central ideal.
acceptance: For G = ℤ_p and n = 1: D_{r_1}(ℤ_p, ℚ_p) = ⊕_{a=0}^{p−1} U_{r_1} δ_a, with δ_p = exp(p log(1 + T)) ∈ U_{r_1}.

sources.locator: Proposition 5.3 and its proof, pp. 17–18
sources.match: Proves that D_r(G, ℚ_p) for r = p^{−1/p^n} is a crossed product of U_r(g) by G/G^{p^n}, computing ‖log(1 + b_i)‖_r = p^{n−1} and the convergence of exp(p^n X_i), and deduces the central quotient version.

nodes.title: The Arens–Michael envelope 𝒰(g) and its coadmissible modules
nodes.statement: Let E/ℚ_p be finite and g the Lie algebra of a linear algebraic group over o_E, with a chosen o_E-basis x_1, …, x_d of the integral Lie lattice g_0 (closed under the bracket). For r ∈ ℝ_{>0} put |Σ_n a_n x^n|_r := sup_n |a_n| r^{|n|} on U(g) (PBW coordinates) and let U(g)_r be the completion; for r ≥ 1 these are Banach algebras. The Arens–Michael envelope is 𝒰(g) := lim_{r≥1} U(g)_r, a Fréchet–Stein algebra and a nuclear Fréchet space; it is the strong dual 𝒪_{G,e}′ of the space of germs at e of analytic functions (an LB-space of compact type), and U(g) → 𝒰(g) is injective with dense image, x ↦ (f ↦ (d/dt) f(exp(tx))|₀). For the small-group analytic distribution algebras D(G_r) (G_r the congruence polydisc subgroups) there are cofinal comparisons: for every r there is r′ with U(g)_{r′} → D(G_r) and D(G_{r′}) → U(g)_r, so 𝒰(g) = lim_r U(g)_r = lim_r D(G_r). A left 𝒰(g)-module is coadmissible in the sense of ND.2/coadmissible-module for the sequence U(g)_r; U(g) → 𝒰(g) and U(g) → U(g)_r are flat, so M ↦ 𝒰(g) ⊗_{U(g)} M is an exact functor from finitely generated U(g)-modules to coadmissible 𝒰(g)-modules. An admissible 𝒰(g)-module is the continuous dual of a coadmissible one, an LB-space of compact type.
hypotheses: Do not confuse 𝒰(g) with the p-adic completion Û(g_R)_K of ND.3/completed-enveloping-algebra: the latter is the single Banach step U(g)_r for the norm of a lattice, while 𝒰(g) is the limit over all radii. BCGP write Û(g) for 𝒰(g).
Left modules; the transition isomorphisms read U(g)_r ⊗_{U(g)_{r+1}} M_{r+1} ≅ M_r.
proofSteps: Submultiplicativity of |·|_r for r ≥ 1 and the description 𝒰(g) = (𝒪_{G,e})′ follow from ST02 Lemmas 2.4–2.5: the germs are power series Σ a_n T^n in coordinates of the second kind with |a_n| s^{|n|} → 0 for some s > 0, their dual is Σ b_n Z^n with sup |b_n| s^{−|n|} < ∞ for all s > 0, and x^n pairs with T^n to give n!·δ (up to the sign convention of ND.1/lie-algebra-in-distributions).

Cofinality with the D(G_r): BCGP Remark 2.2.30; Fréchet–Stein property: BCGP §2.2.29–2.2.30 citing ST03 §3 (the transitions U(g)_{r′} → U(g)_r between Banach completions of an almost commutative algebra are flat, as for Tate algebras of nested polydiscs).

The norms |·|_r, r > 1, are submultiplicative and cofinal among submultiplicative seminorms, so their completion is the Arens–Michael envelope (Schmidt Proposition 3.2.1); 𝒰(g) is a Fréchet–Stein integral domain whose Banach completions are the noetherian U(g)_r, flat over 𝒰(g) (Schmidt Proposition 3.2.3 and the following remark); U(g) → 𝒰(g) is flat (Schmidt Theorem 4.3.3), whence exactness of completion (BCGP Proposition 2.2.35).
acceptance: For g = E·x abelian, U(g)_r = the Tate algebra of the disc |x| ≤ r and 𝒰(g) = 𝒪(𝔸¹), the entire functions; the finitely generated U(g)-module E[x]/(x − a) completes to the coadmissible module 𝒪(𝔸¹)/(x − a) ≅ E for every a ∈ E.

nodes.title: Algebraic microlocalisation of complete filtered rings
nodes.statement: Let A be a ring with an exhaustive separated ℤ-filtration F_•A (F_iA·F_jA ⊆ F_{i+j}A, 1 ∈ F_0A) which is Zariskian (for example complete with noetherian associated graded ring gr A), and let T ⊆ gr A be a (left and right) Ore set of homogeneous elements. Then S := {s ∈ A : gr s ∈ T} is an Ore set in A; the Ore localisation A_S carries a natural Zariskian filtration with gr(A_S) ≅ (gr A)_T; the microlocalisation Q_T(A) is the completion of A_S for that filtration. For a finitely generated A-module M with a good filtration, Q_T(M) is the completion of M_S for the induced good filtration. Then Q_T(A) is flat over A (both sides), Q_T(A) ⊗_A M ≅ Q_T(M), and Q_T(M) = 0 iff M_S = 0, i.e. iff M is S-torsion.
hypotheses: Zariskian filtrations (Li–Van Oystaeyen) are needed for flatness and for the identification Q_T(A) ⊗ M ≅ Q_T(M); a complete filtration with noetherian graded ring is Zariskian (AW13 §2.3).
proofSteps: (a) S is Ore, (b) the induced filtration on A_S is Zariskian with graded ring (gr A)_T, and (c) good filtrations localise: Li–Van Oystaeyen, Corollary 2.2, Propositions 2.3, 2.6, 2.8 and Corollaries 2.4, 2.5, 2.7 of [56] in AW13 (AW13 §2.4, Lemma and Corollary, p. 9).
The Ore localisation itself is Mathlib's OreLocalization for the Ore set S; the filtration and its completion are built on Mathlib's IsRingFiltration and UniformSpace.Completion.
acceptance: For A = ℤ_p[[X]] with its (p, X)-adic filtration and the Ore set of powers of gr p, the microlocalisation is the completed localisation of ℤ_p[[X]] at the elements p^a + (p, X)^{a+1}, which is ℚ_p⟨X/p⟩ (ND.4/lazard-microlocalisation in dimension one).

nodes.title: Lazard's m-adic filtration of the Iwasawa algebra of a uniform group
nodes.statement: Let R be a complete discrete valuation ring with uniformiser p (so R is unramified over ℤ_p) and residue field k, G uniform of dimension d with minimal generators g_i, b_i = g_i − 1, and m = ker(R[[G]] → k) the maximal ideal. Then R[G] is dense in R[[G]], every element is uniquely Σ_α λ_α b^α (λ_α ∈ R), and the m-adic degree is deg(Σ λ_α b^α) = min_α (v(λ_α) + |α|). The m-adic filtration is complete, and gr_m R[[G]] ≅ U(gr G ⊗_{𝔽_p} k) as graded k[t]-algebras, where gr G ⊗ k ≅ t·h_k[t] with h_k = h/ph, h = (1/p) R L_G. In particular gr_m R[[G]] is a noetherian domain, so the m-adic filtration is Zariskian.
hypotheses: The degree formula and the description of gr need p to be a uniformiser; for ramified R the elements p^a + m^{a+1} may include 0 (sourceIssues).
proofSteps: Density and the power-series description: AW13 §10.3, from the proof of DDMS Theorem 7.20 and DDMS Theorem 7.5 for the degree formula; completeness from p-adic completeness of R.

ω(g) = i + 1 on G^{p^i} ∖ G^{p^{i+1}} is a p-valuation whose graded Lie algebra is gr G, because commutators agree modulo G^{p²} with the Lie bracket (DDMS Lemma 4.28); Lazard's Theorem III.2.3.3 gives gr R[[G]] ≅ U(gr G ⊗ k) (AW13 §10.3, proof; Schneider Theorem 28.3).
gr G ⊗ k ≅ t h_k[t] is free of rank d over k[t] (AW13 Lemma 10.2), so the PBW theorem makes U of it a noetherian domain (AW13 Corollary 10.3).
acceptance: For G = ℤ_p (written 1 + pℤ_p), R[[G]] = R[[b]], deg(Σ λ_n b^n) = min(v(λ_n) + n), and gr_m = k[t][σ(b)] with σ(b) of degree 1: the (p, b)-adic filtration of R[[b]].

sources.locator: §10.1, §10.2 Lemma, §10.3 Theorem and Corollary, pp. 67–69
sources.match: With p a uniformiser of R, describes R[[G]] as power series in the b_i, proves Lazard's degree formula and completeness, identifies gr R[[G]] with U(gr G ⊗ k), and shows it is a noetherian domain.
Proves the isomorphism gr O ⊗_{𝔽_p[P]} U(gr G) ≅ gr Λ(G) for p-valued G.

nodes.title: The microlocal Ore set S_0 = ⋃_a (p^a + m^{a+1})
nodes.statement: Under the hypotheses of ND.4/m-adic-filtration (R unramified with uniformiser p), the powers of gr p form a multiplicatively closed set of homogeneous central regular elements of the noetherian domain gr_m R[[G]], hence an Ore set T, and the associated set of ND.4/microlocalisation is S_0 = {x ∈ R[[G]] : gr x = (gr p)^a for some a ≥ 0} = ⋃_{a≥0} (p^a + m^{a+1}). S_0 is an Ore set of R[[G]] not containing 0, and for each n ≥ 0 the analogous set S_n ⊆ R[[G^{p^n}]] is stable under conjugation by G.
hypotheses: Fu (17) takes R to be the integers of an arbitrary finite extension K of ℚ_p; for ramified R, p ∈ m², so 0 = p − p ∈ p + m² and S_0 is not an Ore set of nonzerodivisors. Over ramified K the microlocalisation is obtained by base change (ND.4/microlocal-coefficient-extension).
proofSteps: gr p is central and regular in gr_m R[[G]] (it is t in degree 1 of k[t] ⊆ U(t h_k[t])), so its powers form an Ore set of the noetherian domain; ND.4/microlocalisation (a) transports this to S_0 (AW13 §10.4, the display of S, p. 70).
x ∈ p^a + m^{a+1} has gr x = (gr p)^a because deg p^a = a when p is a uniformiser; the converse is the definition of the symbol.
Conjugation by G preserves the m_n-adic filtration of R[[G^{p^n}]] and fixes p (AW13 §10.6, p. 71).
acceptance: For G = ℤ_p and R = ℤ_p, S_0 contains p + b² but not b + p²: its elements are those whose leading form is a power of p.

sources.locator: §10.4, the definition of S, p. 70, and §10.6, the sets S_n, p. 71

nodes.title: The microlocalisation of R[[G]] is the completed enveloping algebra
nodes.statement: Let R be a complete discrete valuation ring with uniformiser p, K = Frac R, G a uniform pro-p group with minimal generators g_i and h = (1/p) R L_G with R-basis u_i (corresponding to the g_i). The exponential exp(u) converges in A := Û(h)_K for u ∈ L_G ⊆ p h, and g ↦ exp(log g) is an injective group homomorphism G → A^×; it extends to a strictly filtered ring homomorphism ψ : R[[G]] → A with ψ(b_i) = exp(p u_i) − 1 ≡ p u_i, sending gr p to the invertible symbol s and gr b_i to s u_i. The induced map from the microlocalisation is an isomorphism of complete ℤ-filtered rings Q_{gr p}(R[[G]]) ≅ Û(h)_K. Consequently K[[G]] → Û(h)_K is flat (both sides) and, for finitely generated K[[G]]-modules M, Û(h)_K ⊗_{K[[G]]} M = 0 iff M is S_0-torsion. For n ≥ 0, Q_{gr p}(R[[G^{p^n}]]) ≅ Û(h)_{n,K}.
hypotheses: R unramified over ℤ_p (p a uniformiser); the ramified case is ND.4/microlocal-coefficient-extension.
The microlocalisation already inverts p (p ∈ S_0): the target is the rational algebra Û(h)_K, not the integral completion Û(h).
proofSteps: The Campbell–Hausdorff formula (DDMS Theorem 6.28) shows u ∗ v = log(exp u exp v) ∈ L_G, and u ↦ exp u identifies G with exp(L_G) ⊂ A^× (AW13 §10.4, proof, citing the proof of DDMS Theorem 9.10).

ψ(b^α) ≡ p^{|α|} u^α mod p^{|α|+1} F_0 A, so with Lazard's degree formula (ND.4/m-adic-filtration) and the PBW basis of the slice gr_0 A ≅ U(h_k), deg ψ(x) = deg x on R[G]; ψ extends by density to a strictly filtered map on R[[G]].

gr A ≅ U(h_k)[s, s^{−1}] (AW13 Lemma 3.1), so ψ extends to Q_t(R[[G]]) by the universal property of microlocalisation (ND.4/microlocalisation); it is injective (strictly filtered) and its graded map is surjective, hence it is an isomorphism of complete filtered rings (AW13 Theorem 10.4, proof, pp. 70–71).
Flatness and the torsion criterion are ND.4/microlocalisation. The statement for G^{p^n} uses L_{G^{p^n}} = p^n L_G (AW13 Proposition 10.6(a)).
acceptance: For G = 1 + pℤ_p ≅ ℤ_p and R = ℤ_p, Q_{gr p}(ℤ_p[[b]]) ≅ ℚ_p⟨u⟩ with b ↦ exp(pu) − 1: the microlocalisation is the Tate algebra of the disc |b| ≤ |p|.
Lazard's original form: Û(h) is the saturation Sat(R[G]) of the valued group ring (AW13 Remark 10.5(a)).

nodes.title: The Banach step D_{1/p}(G, K) is the completed enveloping algebra
nodes.statement: Let p be odd, L/ℚ_p finite, K a complete discretely valued extension of L with integers R, and G an L-uniform group with associated R-Lie algebra g = R ⊗_{o_L} (1/p) L_G. There is a natural isomorphism of K-Banach algebras D_{1/p}(G, K) ≅ Û(g)_K, extending the map g ↦ exp(log g) on G ⊂ D(G, K). For L = ℚ_p, D_{1/p}(G, K) consists of the series Σ d_α b^α with |d_α| p^{−|α|} → 0.
hypotheses: p odd and G uniform (L-uniform for general L).

The isomorphism is of Banach algebras with the norm ‖·‖_{1/p} on the left and the π-adic norm of the lattice Û(g) on the right; AW14 Lemma 5.2 writes the coefficient condition as finiteness of the supremum (sourceIssues: the completion requires decay to zero).
proofSteps: For K′ ⊆ K unramified over ℚ_p with K/K′ finite (Cohen structure theorem), the Lazard microlocalisation theorem (ND.4/lazard-microlocalisation, AW13 Theorem 10.4) identifies Q_{gr p}(R′G) with Û(g′)_{K′}; both sides are the completion of K′[G] for ‖·‖_{1/p} (AW14 Lemma 5.2, proof, p. 14; AW13 Remark 10.5(c)).
Base change to K: Û(g)_K = K ⊗_{K′} Û(g′)_{K′} (ND.3/completed-enveloping-algebra) and D_{1/p}(G, K) = K ⊗_{K′} D_{1/p}(G, K′) from the coefficient description (ND.2/banach-steps).
For general L, restriction of scalars from L to ℚ_p and the quotient D(G_0, K) → D(G, K) (AW14 Lemma 5.2, end of proof).
acceptance: For G = 1 + pℤ_p ≅ ℤ_p, D_{1/p}(ℤ_p, ℚ_p) ≅ ℚ_p⟨u⟩ with u = log(1 + T)/p: the Tate algebra in u.

nodes.title: Microlocalisation over a ramified coefficient field
nodes.statement: Let K be a finite extension of ℚ_p with integers R (possibly ramified), G uniform, and g_{ℤ_p} = (1/p) L_G. Define the microlocalisation of K[[G]] = K ⊗_{ℚ_p} ℚ_p[[G]] as the base change K ⊗_{ℚ_p} (ℚ_p[[G]] → Û(g_{ℤ_p})_{ℚ_p}) of ND.4/lazard-microlocalisation. Then Û(g_{ℤ_p})_{ℚ_p} ⊗_{ℚ_p} K ≅ Û(g_R)_K with g_R = R ⊗ g_{ℤ_p}, the resulting map K[[G]] → Û(g_R)_K is flat on both sides, it is the unique continuous extension of g ↦ exp(log g), and for a K[[G]]-module M, Û(g_R)_K ⊗_{K[[G]]} M ≅ Û(g_{ℤ_p})_{ℚ_p} ⊗_{ℚ_p[[G]]} M, where M is viewed as a ℚ_p[[G]]-module by restriction.
hypotheses: This replaces Fu's direct use of the set (17) over ramified R (sourceIssues, Fu E4); the microlocal Ore set is used only over ℤ_p.
proofSteps: Base change of completed enveloping algebras along finite K/ℚ_p: ND.3/completed-enveloping-algebra (AW13 Lemma 3.9).
Flatness is preserved by base change: K ⊗ Û(g_{ℤ_p})_{ℚ_p} is flat over K ⊗ ℚ_p[[G]] = K[[G]] (Bourbaki, Commutative Algebra I §2.7).
Agreement with exp(log g) holds on G ⊂ K[[G]], which is dense; continuity gives uniqueness.
For the module formula write B = K ⊗ Û, A = K ⊗ ℚ_p[[G]] and Λ = ℚ_p[[G]]; then B = A ⊗_Λ Û, so B ⊗_A M ≅ Û ⊗_Λ M for every A-module M (associativity of tensor products).
acceptance: For K = ℚ_p this is ND.4/lazard-microlocalisation with R = ℤ_p.

nodes.title: Microlocalisation of finitely generated Iwasawa modules
nodes.statement: For K finite over ℚ_p, G uniform and M a finitely generated K[[G]]-module, its microlocalisation is M̂ := Û(g_K) ⊗_{K[[G]]} M with the natural K[[G]]-linear map η_M : M → M̂, m ↦ 1 ⊗ m. The functor M ↦ M̂ is exact (flatness, ND.4/microlocal-coefficient-extension), natural in M, sends finitely generated modules to finitely generated Û(g_K)-modules, and M̂ = 0 iff M is S_0-torsion (over K = ℚ_p; over general K after restriction to ℚ_p[[G]]). Microlocalisation is not faithful: S_0-torsion modules are killed; faithful flatness of K[[G]] → D(G, K) (ND.2/faithful-flatness) is a different statement.
proofSteps: Exactness and the torsion criterion are ND.4/microlocalisation and ND.4/lazard-microlocalisation; finite generation is preserved by base change of finitely generated modules.
acceptance: M = K[[G]] gives M̂ = Û(g_K); for M = K (trivial module) M̂ = K, since the augmentation of every s ∈ S_0 is a nonzero element of p^a(1 + pR), so S_0 acts invertibly on the trivial module.

nodes.title: Lie modules: semisimplicity and the equivalence with finite-dimensional g-modules
nodes.statement: Let R be unramified with uniformiser p, G a uniform group which is a congruence kernel ker(𝔾(ℤ_p) → 𝔾(ℤ/p^{m+1})) of a semisimple group scheme 𝔾 over R with Lie algebra 𝔤, p^{m+1}𝔤 = R ⊗ L_G, and U_n = Q_{gr p}(R[[G^{p^n}]]) ≅ Û(𝔤)_{n+m,K} with crossed products U_n ∗ H_n, H_n = G/G^{p^n}. Let ℳ be the category of K[[G]]-modules finite-dimensional over K. (P) If M ∈ ℳ is S_n-torsion-free, η_M : M → (U_n ∗ H_n) ⊗_{K[[G]]} M is an isomorphism; every M ∈ ℳ is S_n-torsion-free for n large. (a) ℳ is semisimple. (b) The Lie modules ℒ ⊆ ℳ (restrictions of finite-dimensional U_0-modules along K[[G]] → U_0) are equivalent, via U_0 ⊗_{K[[G]]} −, to finite-dimensional U(𝔤_K)-modules; a simple Lie module V has End_{K[[G]]}(V) = K. (c) Every simple M ∈ ℳ is V ⊗ ρ with V a simple Lie module and ρ a simple Artin module (some open subgroup acts trivially).
hypotheses: The semisimplicity and lattice hypotheses of AW13 §10.12 are part of the statement. The very-good-prime restriction of §10.12 is not needed: AW13 §11.1 drops it. For a uniform group with nonsemisimple Lie algebra the conclusion (a) fails: for G = ℤ_p with topological generator γ, K[[G]]/((γ − 1)²) is a nonsplit extension of the trivial module by itself.
proofSteps: (P) for n = 0: a finite-dimensional S-torsion-free module is unchanged by localisation at S, because s acts injectively hence bijectively, and its R-lattice is already p-adically complete (AW13 Proposition 11.1, proof, using Li–Van Oystaeyen I.5.5 for separation); general n by restriction to G^{p^n} and the crossed-product identity (U_n ∗ H_n) ⊗ M ≅ U_n ⊗_{R G^{p^n}} M (AW13 Proposition 10.6(d)). Torsion-freeness for n large: AW13 Corollary 10.11.

(a): identify V with a module over U_n ∗ H_n; finite-dimensional U_n-modules are semisimple (AW13 Corollary 9.2), and averaging a U_n-linear projection over H_n in characteristic zero gives a K[[G]]-linear one (AW13 Theorem 11.1(a), citing Passman).
(b): restriction and base change are adjoint, and (P) with n = 0 shows the unit and counit are isomorphisms on Lie modules (AW13 Theorem 11.1(b)); End = K by Corollary 11.1.
(c): AW13 Theorem 11.2 (factorisation), using isotypy of (U_n ∗ H_n) ⊗ M as a U_n-module (Lemma 11.2).
acceptance: For G = G_1 ⊂ SL_2(ℤ_p) (m = 0, p odd), the finite-dimensional ℚ_p[[G_1]]-modules are semisimple and Sym^k(ℚ_p²) is a simple Lie module.

nodes.title: The Lie module attached to a finite-dimensional representation
nodes.statement: Let K be finite over ℚ_p with integers R, G uniform with g_R = (1/p)R L_G and g_K split semisimple. Let W be a finite-dimensional U(g_K)-module and W_0 ⊆ W a g_R-stable R-lattice. The U(g_R)-action on W_0 extends continuously to Û(g_R) (W_0 is finite free, hence p-adically complete), hence the U(g_K)-action on W extends to Û(g_K); pulling back along the microlocalisation K[[G]] → Û(g_K) (ND.4/microlocal-coefficient-extension) makes W a K[[G]]-module 𝓛(W), a Lie module. Its restriction to G is the representation g ↦ exp(log g) acting on W, and its differentiated action is the given g_K-action. If W is irreducible, 𝓛(W) is irreducible, and End_{K[[G]]}(𝓛(W)) = K.
hypotheses: A g_R-stable lattice exists for every finite-dimensional W (AW13 §9.2, via Humphreys' lattice argument); the K[[G]]-module 𝓛(W) does not depend on its choice.
proofSteps: Continuity of the U(g_R)-action for the p-adic topology of W_0 gives the extension to Û(g_R) and Û(g_K) (Fu §4, p. 14; AW13 §9.2).
Independence of the lattice: two lattices are commensurable, and the extended actions agree on the dense subalgebra U(g_K).
Irreducibility and End = K: ND.4/lie-modules (b).
acceptance: For G = G_1 ⊂ SL_2(ℤ_p) and W = Sym^k(ℚ_p²) with lattice Sym^k(ℤ_p²), 𝓛(W) is the restriction to G_1 of the algebraic representation of SL_2(ℤ_p) (ND.6/algebraic-peter-weyl).

nodes.title: Microlocalisation preserves W-isotypic quotients
nodes.statement: Let K be finite over ℚ_p, G uniform with g_K split semisimple and satisfying the hypotheses of ND.4/lie-modules, W an irreducible finite-dimensional g_K-module with stable lattice, viewed as a Lie module. Write Ann(W) ⊆ U(g_K), Ânn(W) ⊆ Û(g_K) and Ãnn(W) ⊆ K[[G]] for the annihilators, and for a finitely generated K[[G]]-module M put M_W = M/Ãnn(W)M and M̂_W = M̂/Ânn(W)M̂ (the maximal quotients isomorphic to finite sums of W). Then U(g_K)/Ann(W) ≅ Û(g_K)/Ânn(W) ≅ End_K(W), and for every finitely generated K[[G]]-module M the natural map M_W → M̂_W is an isomorphism, naturally in M. In particular K[[G]]/Ãnn(W) ≅ Û(g_K)/Ânn(W) ≅ End_K(W).
hypotheses: Surjectivity of K[[G]]/Ãnn(W) → End_K(W) is part of the conclusion: a priori the map is only injective; it follows from the comparison, not from irreducibility of W over an arbitrary field.
proofSteps: U(g_K)/Ann(W) ≅ End_K(W) by the density theorem for the absolutely irreducible module W over the split semisimple g_K (Fu (19), citing Bourbaki VIII §6.2), and U(g_K) is dense in Û(g_K), which acts through the same finite-dimensional quotient.

Apply the flat functor M ↦ M̂ to 0 → Ãnn(W)M → M → M_W → 0. M_W is a finite sum of W, hence S_0-torsion-free with S_0 acting invertibly (S_0 consists of units of Û(g_K)), so by ND.4/lie-modules (P) with n = 0, M_W ≅ Û ⊗ M_W, compatibly with the reverse Û-linear map (Fu, proof of Theorem 4.3, p. 15). For ramified K, (P) is applied over ℚ_p: by ND.4/microlocal-coefficient-extension, Û(g_K) ⊗_{K[[G]]} M_W ≅ Û(g_{ℤ_p})_{ℚ_p} ⊗_{ℚ_p[[G]]} M_W, and M_W restricted to ℚ_p[[G]] is finite-dimensional and S_0-torsion-free.
Maximality of M̂_W gives Ânn(W)M̂ ⊆ Û ⊗ Ãnn(W)M, and Û·Ãnn(W) ⊆ Ânn(W) gives the reverse inclusion; hence M̂_W = M_W.
acceptance: For M = K[[G]], the theorem gives K[[G]]/Ãnn(W) ≅ End_K(W), the identity used in Fu (32) for W = W_k.

nodes.title: Central specialisations of distribution and enveloping algebras
nodes.statement: Let G be a compact open subgroup of 𝔾(ℚ_p) for a connected split reductive ℚ_p-group 𝔾 with Lie algebra g, Z(g) the centre of U(g), K/ℚ_p finite and λ : Z(g) → K a character; for generators z_1, …, z_n of the polynomial ring Z(g), ker λ is generated by z_1 − λ(z_1), …, z_n − λ(z_n). Define: D(G, K)_λ := D(G, K) ⊗_{Z(g), λ} K = D(G, K)/Σ_i D(G, K)(z_i − λ(z_i)); C^la(G, K)[λ] := {f ∈ C^an(G, K) : z f = λ(z) f for all z ∈ Z(g)}, z acting through ND.1/central-enveloping-distributions; and similarly D^λ_r(G, K) := D_r(G, K)/D_r(G, K)·ker λ, U^λ_r(g) := U_r(g)/U_r(g)·ker λ and Û(g)_λ := Û(g_K)/Û(g_K)·ker λ. The ideal Σ D(G, K)(z_i − λ(z_i)) is a closed two-sided ideal, so D(G, K)_λ is a Fréchet–Stein algebra and a coadmissible D(G, K)-module, and C^la(G, K)[λ] is a closed G-stable subspace of C^an(G, K), of compact type. For 𝔾 = SL_2^m, Z(g) = K[Δ_1, …, Δ_m] with Δ_i = ½h_i² − h_i + 2e_if_i, and λ is determined by λ = (λ(Δ_i))_i ∈ K^m.
hypotheses: Fu writes the kernel of λ on Z(g) through p²Δ + λ_0, so that λ_0 = −p²λ(Δ) in his notation; this roadmap writes λ = λ(Δ) directly.
Closedness of the ideal uses that it is finitely generated and two-sided (z_i central); a non-closed ideal would not give a Fréchet quotient.
proofSteps: The z_i − λ(z_i) are central (ND.1/central-enveloping-distributions), so the left ideal they generate is two-sided; finitely generated left ideals of a Fréchet–Stein algebra are closed (ND.2/coadmissible-theorems), and quotients by closed two-sided ideals are Fréchet–Stein (ST03 Proposition 3.7).

C^la(G, K)[λ] is the joint kernel of the continuous operators z_i − λ(z_i), hence closed; closed subspaces of spaces of compact type are of compact type (LocallyAnalyticDistributions:L0/compact-type-spaces); G-stability holds because z_i acts G-equivariantly.
For sl_2, Z(U(sl_2)) = K[Δ] by Harish-Chandra (LieHighestWeight Layer 7); for a product, Z is the tensor product of the centres.
acceptance: On W_k = Sym^k(K²), Δ acts by ½k(k + 2); so W_k is a quotient of D(G_1, K)_λ for λ = ½k(k + 2).

nodes.title: Induced infinitesimal characters
nodes.statement: In the setting of ND.5/infinitesimal-character-quotients, fix a Borel pair (𝔹, 𝕋) of 𝔾 with T = 𝕋(ℚ_p) ∩ G, B = 𝔹(ℚ_p) ∩ G = TN, and a triangular decomposition g_0 = n̄_0 ⊕ t_0 ⊕ n_0; let HC : Z(g) → U(t) be the Harish-Chandra homomorphism for this decomposition. A locally analytic character χ : T → 1 + pℤ_p has derivative dχ : U(t) → ℚ_p. An infinitesimal character λ : Z(g) → ℚ_p is induced if λ = dχ ∘ HC for some such χ. For 𝔾 = SL_2 and G = G_1, a character χ(diag(t, t⁻¹)) = t^c (c ∈ ℤ_p) gives λ(Δ) = ½c² + c, so λ is induced iff 2λ(Δ) + 1 is the square of an element of ℤ_p; for G = G_1^m, iff each 2λ_i + 1 is a square in ℤ_p.
hypotheses: The sign of the linear term in λ(Δ) = ½c² ± c depends on the choice of n versus n̄; the criterion '2λ(Δ) + 1 is a square in ℤ_p' does not.
Fu Remark 5.8 asserts that λ is induced iff v_p(λ_0) ≥ 2; only the 'only if' direction holds (sourceIssues).
proofSteps: For SL_2, T ∩ G_1 = {diag(t, t⁻¹) : t ∈ 1 + pℤ_p} ≅ ℤ_p, and every continuous character to 1 + pℤ_p is t ↦ t^c, c ∈ ℤ_p, with dχ(h) = c.
HC(Δ) = ½h² + h (or ½h² − h for the opposite Borel), so λ(Δ) = ½c² ± c and 2λ(Δ) + 1 = (c ± 1)², a square in ℤ_p; conversely if 2λ + 1 = s², s ∈ ℤ_p, take c = s − 1.
acceptance: λ_k(Δ) = ½k(k + 2) for W_k is induced (c = k).
At p = 3, λ(Δ) = 1 is integral but not induced: 2·1 + 1 = 3 is not a square in ℚ_3.

sources.locator: §5, the Harish-Chandra homomorphism (24) and the definition of induced characters, p. 16; Remark 5.8, pp. 20–21
sources.match: Defines induced infinitesimal characters λ = dχ ∘ HC for analytic torus characters χ : T → 1 + pℤ_p and claims a valuation criterion for being induced.

uses.how: the direct proof of injectivity uses the locally analytic principal series of an induced character
genericity is needed only at the induced parameters λ_k

nodes.title: Strong duality after infinitesimal specialisation
nodes.statement: In the setting of ND.5/infinitesimal-character-quotients with K = ℚ_p (or K finite over ℚ_p), the pairing D(G, K) × C^an(G, K) → K induces a topological isomorphism of Fréchet spaces D(G, K)_λ ≅ (C^la(G, K)[λ])′_b. Equivalently, the annihilator of C^la(G, K)[λ] in D(G, K) is the closed ideal D(G, K)·ker λ.
hypotheses: G compact open in the ℚ_p-points of a connected split reductive group, so that Z(g) acts centrally and G-equivariantly.
proofSteps: The z_i − λ(z_i) act by continuous G-equivariant endomorphisms of C^an(G, K) (ND.1/central-enveloping-distributions), giving the strict left exact sequence 0 → C^la(G, K)[λ] → C^an(G, K) → C^an(G, K)^n, f ↦ ((z_i − λ(z_i))f)_i (Fu (25)–(26)).

Dualise: for spaces of compact type the strong dual is exact on strict sequences and the closed subspace C^la[λ] has dual the quotient of D(G, K) by its annihilator (LocallyAnalyticDistributions:L0/compact-type-nuclear-duality and L0/compact-type-extension-duality, with Hahn–Banach over the spherically complete K).

The annihilator is the closure of the image of the transposed map D(G, K)^n → D(G, K), (μ_i) ↦ Σ μ_i(z_i − λ(z_i)) (up to the antipode, which preserves Z(g)); that image is the finitely generated ideal D(G, K)·ker λ, closed by ND.2/coadmissible-theorems. Fu obtains the same identification from ST03 Theorem 6.3.
acceptance: For λ = λ_k, W_k^* ⊗ W_k ⊆ C^la(G, K)[λ_k] (matrix coefficients, ND.6/algebraic-peter-weyl), and dually D(G, K)_{λ_k} surjects onto End_K(W_k).

sources.locator: Theorem 5.2, first assertion, and its proof, equations (25)–(26), p. 16

nodes.title: The locally analytic principal series and a nowhere-vanishing eigenfunction
nodes.statement: In the setting of ND.5/induced-infinitesimal-characters, for a locally analytic character χ : T → 1 + pℤ_p let Ind(χ) := {f ∈ C^an(G, ℚ_p) : f(gtn) = χ(t) f(g) for g ∈ G, t ∈ T, n ∈ N}, a closed G-stable subspace (G acting by left translation). Z(g) acts on Ind(χ) by the induced character λ = dχ ∘ HC, so Ind(χ) ⊆ C^la(G, ℚ_p)[λ]. Choosing a locally analytic section of G → X := G/B over a finite disjoint open cover of X, one obtains a topological isomorphism Ind(χ) ≅ C^an(X, ℚ_p) and a function f_0 ∈ Ind(χ) with f_0(g) ≠ 0 for every g ∈ G; then f_0·φ ∈ C^la(G, ℚ_p)[λ] for every smooth (locally constant) φ on G.
hypotheses: The section is locally analytic on a finite disjoint cover, not a single global analytic section of the flag variety; this suffices because X is compact and totally disconnected.
Z(g) acts on C^an(G, ℚ_p) by differential operators, which are local: on each open set where φ is constant, z(φ f_0) = φ·z(f_0).
proofSteps: X = G/B is a compact ℚ_p-analytic manifold and G → X is a locally trivial B-bundle with locally analytic sections over a finite disjoint open cover (LocallyAnalyticDistributions:L0/analytic-manifold-atlases); Ind(χ) ≅ C^an(X, ℚ_p) by restricting along the section (Fu, proof of Theorem 5.2, p. 17).
Take f_0 the function equal to 1 on the image of the section, extended by f_0(s(x)tn) = χ(t); it never vanishes since χ takes values in 1 + pℤ_p.

Z(g) acts on Ind(χ) through dχ ∘ HC: in the triangular PBW decomposition z = HC(z) + (terms ending in n), right N-invariance kills the second part and right T-equivariance makes U(t) act through dχ (Fu, p. 16, after the definition of Ind(χ)); multiplication by a locally constant function commutes with differential operators on each open set where it is constant.
acceptance: For χ trivial, Ind(χ) = C^an(G/B, ℚ_p) and f_0 = 1; λ = HC^*(0) is the infinitesimal character of the trivial representation.

sources.locator: §5, the definition of Ind(χ), p. 16, and the proof of Theorem 5.2, second part, p. 17
sources.match: Defines the locally analytic principal series, uses a splitting X ↪ G ↠ X to identify Ind(χ) with C^la(X, ℚ_p), and chooses a nowhere-vanishing f_0 with infinitesimal character λ.

uses.how: f_0 times smooth functions is a dense subspace of C(G, ℚ_p) inside C^la[λ]
